about.title: Mission Viejo Workplace Injury Claims
about.longDescription: A workday in Mission Viejo can end in an urgent care lobby instead of your own driveway. Some injuries happen inside a warehouse, a medical office, a retail stockroom, or on a residential remodel. Others happen behind the wheel: employees who drive for work share I-5, Marguerite Parkway, Alicia Parkway, and Los Alisos Boulevard with everyone else, and in 2025 the city logged 210 injury collisions in which 289 people were hurt. Under California law, workers' compensation usually pays for a job injury no matter who was at fault, and it is normally your only claim against your employer. That is not always where things stop. When a subcontractor, a property owner, an equipment manufacturer, or another driver caused the harm, a separate third-party claim may exist alongside your comp benefits. LawProactive is a free service, not a law firm. We connect Orange County workers with an independent attorney who can sort out which paths apply to you and explain the deadline attached to each.

whyChoose.title: Why Mission Viejo Workers Turn to LawProactive

items.title: Comp is not always the whole picture
items.desc: Workers' compensation is usually your exclusive remedy against your employer, but an attorney in our network can look for a negligent third party, such as a subcontractor, property owner, equipment maker, or another driver, who may owe you more.

items.title: Deadlines handled early
items.desc: California expects you to report a work injury to your employer within 30 days, and a third-party claim generally carries a two-year filing deadline. Getting connected quickly helps keep both clocks in view.

items.title: No cost to connect, no fee without recovery
items.desc: LawProactive charges nothing to match you with an independent attorney, and the attorneys in our network work on contingency. Retaliation for reporting an injury is illegal in California, and a lawyer can speak up if your employer pushes back.

items.question: I was rear-ended on Alicia Parkway while making deliveries for my job. Is that a workers' comp case or a car accident case?
items.answer: It can be both. Because you were working at the time, workers' compensation generally covers your medical care and part of your lost wages regardless of who caused the crash. The other driver is a third party, so you may also have a separate injury claim against them and their insurer. An attorney can explain how the two claims interact so one does not undercut the other.

items.question: What happens if I wait too long to tell my employer I got hurt?
items.answer: California asks you to report a job injury to your employer within 30 days. Missing that window can complicate your workers' comp benefits, though it does not always end the claim. If you are unsure whether you reported in time or how to do it properly, that is a good reason to speak with an attorney sooner rather than later.

items.question: Can my Mission Viejo employer fire me or cut my hours for filing a claim?
items.answer: No. Retaliating against a worker for reporting an injury or filing a workers' compensation claim is illegal in California. If you notice a sudden change in schedule, pay, or treatment after you reported, write down what happened and when. An attorney connected through LawProactive can review whether those actions cross the line.
